# 22 comments red the guard CI runs, so any PR touching those files fails on a line it did not write

## Context

CI runs the published archaeology binary; the pre-commit hook runs the engine's mirrored copy, and the two disagree (#18809). The practical consequence is not abstract: **22 comments in this repository are flagged by the guard CI runs and passed by the hook**, so any PR that stages one of those files reds on a line it did not write.

That has already happened twice today — PR #18793 (a prose `pull request 11982` in a file I touched for an unrelated reason) and PR #18808 (`RA-3`, same shape). Both cost a full CI cycle and an unrelated repair inside someone else's PR.

Measured at `origin/dev` with the installed `neo-agent-skills@0.1.8` binary, restricted to trees this repo's guard scans:

Live latest-open sweep 2026-09-16T18:55Z: only #18809 (the divergence itself) and #18794. A2A sweep of the latest 30: no competing claim.

## The Problem

Four kinds, and the distinction is the work — a blanket suppression would hide all four equally:

**A · A deliberate ref carrying the RETIRED marker (3 sites).** `ticket-ref-ok` was retired and CI rejects it, but these refs are genuinely load-bearing — the ticket a script implements.
`check-branch-discipline.mjs:9`, `:56` (`#11133`) · `mergedPullRequestPush.mjs:30` (`#16256`)

**B · Review archaeology (3 sites).** Which review round produced a decision — the class that decays fastest, and the one family with **no escape at all**.
`DockSplitterPaint.spec.mjs:130` (`RA-2`) · `GallerySortSelection.spec.mjs:228` (`Cycle-1 RA1`) · `dockRailTabLayering.spec.mjs:20` (*"in review on PR 17524"*)

**C · Not a reference at all (11 sites).** Ordinal labels the numeric pattern cannot distinguish from a ticket.
`RefreshDomCorpseRepro.spec.mjs` ×6 (`Refresh #1` / `#2`) · `DockDragDropNL.spec.mjs:49,77` (`product truth #1` / `#2`) · `MultiWriterNL.spec.mjs:70` (`identity #1`)

**D · Genuine decay-prone ticket refs (5 sites).** Real citations that rot when the item closes or is renamed.
`calendar/view/month/Component.mjs:740,755` (`todo: #989`, `#990`) · `grid/VerticalScrollbar.mjs:24` (`#3`) · `util/KeyNavigation.mjs:71` (`#64`) · `CrossLinkIssuesUrl.spec.mjs:22` (`#12209`) · `PoolingRuntimeUpdates.spec.mjs:5` (`#9165`)

## The Architectural Reality

The typed escape `[not-ticket-ref: <reason>]` binds to a **bare `#N`** and works today — verified against the installed 0.1.8 binary, not reasoned from the regex. So A and C are declarable in place. B has no escape in any version (`neo-agent-skills#83` covers the named-ref families; review archaeology is explicitly out of scope there), so it must be rephrased. D is a judgment call per site: rephrase to describe the behaviour, or declare the ref deliberate where the pointer genuinely is the contract.

## The Fix

Per site, with the kind stated:

- **A** → the typed marker, same reason text the retired one carried.
- **B** → rephrase. The round number is the only part that decays; what the arm asserts and why is behaviour and stays.
- **C** → the typed marker with `ordinal label, not a ticket`. These are the cheapest and the most valuable to mark, because they are the ones a future reader would otherwise "fix" by deleting a true statement.
- **D** → default to rephrasing. Where the pointer is load-bearing (an open `todo:` naming the work), the typed marker with a reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `neo-agent-skills-ticket-archaeology` reports **zero** findings over this repository's tracked `.mjs`, run as CI runs it.
- [ ] AC-2: every change states its kind — no site is silenced without a reason a reader can disagree with.
- [ ] AC-3: no behaviour change; `git diff -U0` carries no line outside a comment.
- [ ] AC-4: the `todo:` refs in `calendar/view/month/Component.mjs` still name their work — a repair that loses an open todo's subject is a regression in the comment's job.
- [ ] AC-5: full `unit` tier green.

## Out of Scope

- **The mirror divergence itself** (#18809) and its placement decision. This repairs the sites; it does not choose which guard the hook runs.
- The engine copy's missing review-archaeology patterns — that is #18809's safe half and lands separately.
- Rewriting either guard's rules.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not blanket-suppress.** Four kinds with four correct remedies; one marker over all of them hides the three genuine ticket refs behind the eleven false positives.
- ⛔ **Do not delete category D outright.** `#9165` and `#12209` say which regression a suite reproduces — that is the spec's reason for existing, and it needs rephrasing into behaviour rather than removal.
- ⛔ **Do not verify with the local guard.** It passes all 22 today; that is the defect, not the verification. Use `./node_modules/.bin/neo-agent-skills-ticket-archaeology`.
- ⛔ **Do not escape a review-archaeology hit.** There is no escape for that family; a marker there produces `invalid-escape` on top of the original finding.

* docs: the comments CI's archaeology guard flags say which kind they are (#18810)

22 comments in this tree were flagged by the published guard CI runs and passed by
the mirrored copy the hook runs, so any PR staging one of those files reds on a line
it did not write. That happened twice today, in PRs whose subject was elsewhere.

Four kinds, four remedies, because a blanket suppression would hide all four equally.

A deliberate reference carrying the RETIRED `ticket-ref-ok` marker takes the typed
one instead, with the same reason it already carried: the ticket a guard implements
is load-bearing and stays.

Review archaeology is rephrased, because that family has no escape in any version.
Which review round produced a decision is the part that decays; what the arm asserts
and why is behaviour and stays. `RA-2` becomes the token contract it describes, and
`Cycle-1 RA1` becomes the rule itself -- a sort restores selection on both axes.

Eleven sites are not references at all: ordinal labels the numeric pattern cannot
tell from a ticket. `Refresh #1`, `product truth #2`, `identity #1`. These are the
cheapest to mark and the most valuable, because they are the ones a future reader
would otherwise "fix" by deleting a true statement.

`VerticalScrollbar`'s `To solve #3` was nearly one of those deletions. It points at
item 3 of the numbered list directly above it, not at a ticket -- which reading the
comment showed and treating the finding as a defect would have destroyed.

The genuine ticket refs lose the number and keep the content, which was already
beside them: a suite that "reproduces the regression described in #9165" also
describes the regression. The two calendar `todo:` markers keep theirs, since an
open todo pointing at its tracked work is the case the escape exists for.

Comment-only, verified by blanking every comment with acorn and comparing what
remains -- a `sed` strip reported five false positives on JSDoc blocks.

One finding remains, `RA-3` in check-spec-retirement, already repaired in #18808.
